memo.headline: Since 7 October, iOS checkout in Amsterdam and Berlin has been converting at about a third of its usual rate, falling from 65–66% to 21–23% of checkouts becoming orders. That has cost about €90k of first-party revenue in 19 days (about €4.7k a day) and is still happening. It also explains the whole year-on-year revenue decline. New York's €114k drop is seasonal, not a problem.

data_sufficiency.explanation: There are 28 days of first-party sales across 12 markets, with more than 13 months of history, so year-on-year comparisons work. The main findings rest on large samples: thousands of iOS checkouts per market and more than 500k impressions per Meta ad. All of them passed significance after correcting for the number of segments scanned. Weaker spots: (1) brand-search incrementality comes from one 14-day pause in Milan. (2) Mexico City has only 8 weeks of history and small product capacity. (3) There are no margin or cost-of-goods figures, so ROAS cannot yet be turned into profit.

kpis.note: -12.5% on the previous 28 days. Comparing like-for-like markets with the same period last year, it is -3.5% (€1,866,699 vs €1,934,115). Without Berlin and Amsterdam it is +1.3%.

kpis.name: Ad spend
kpis.note: +3.3%. Most of the increase is Barcelona (+€3.1k) and Mexico City (+€3.1k).

kpis.name: Paid first-party revenue
kpis.note: -17%. The biggest falls are New York (seasonal), London, Berlin and Amsterdam.

kpis.name: Paid ROAS (first-party)
kpis.note: Platforms claim €1.31M against €1.02M first-party (1.28x overall; TikTok 1.70x, Meta 1.35x, Google 1.08x).

kpis.name: Orders
kpis.note: -12.6%. New York accounts for -1,829 and Berlin plus Amsterdam for -1,907.

kpis.name: iOS checkout-to-order, Amsterdam + Berlin (7–25 Oct)
kpis.note: Last 7 days: 22.9%. Android and desktop in the same markets are unchanged.

findings.title: iOS checkout broke on 7 Oct in Amsterdam and Berlin: about €90k lost so far, about €4.7k a day
findings.evidence: Amsterdam iOS checkout-to-order fell from 64.7% (1,075/1,661, 16 Sep–6 Oct) to 23.0% (341/1,484, 7–25 Oct). Berlin fell from 66.0% (1,385/2,099) to 20.6% (370/1,800). Both drops are significant after correcting for 36 market×device comparisons (p≈0). The break happened overnight on 7 Oct in both markets (Amsterdam 66% on 6 Oct, 23% on 7 Oct; Berlin 61%, then 16%) and was still there on 19–25 Oct. Berlin Android, used as a control, did not move: 63.5% to 63.4%, no detectable difference. Checkout volume per day is unchanged, so traffic and demand are intact; orders are failing at the last step. At the old rate we would have expected about 619 more orders in Amsterdam (≈€38.6k at a €62.35 average order) and about 818 more in Berlin (≈€50.9k). Year on year, Berlin went from +2.3% in the week of 28 Sep to -39.5% in the week of 12 Oct, and Amsterdam from -8.3% to -29.9%. Every channel fell in proportion, which points to the site, not marketing. Berlin Edition 28 closes at 88.6% sold, the lowest of any market.

findings.title: Madrid 'Autumn special' will leave about €110k of capacity unsold unless it is pushed now
findings.evidence: 808 of 2,837 sold (28.5%) with 77.4% of the selling window gone and 12 days left (ends 6 Nov). The last 7 days sold 126 units (18 a day). At that pace it reaches about 1,024, leaving about 1,813 units × €60.64 ≈ €110k unsold. Madrid's regular editions 18–27 all sold 91–99% of capacity. Madrid has also used only 76.6% of its October budget with 80.6% of the month gone, about €900 below pace.

findings.title: Paris 'Video A' (PAR-META-1) is fatigued: frequency rose from 1.85 to 5.29 and CTR halved
findings.evidence: Weekly CTR went 1.42% → 1.31% → 1.16% → 0.95% → 0.77% → 0.65% as frequency rose from 1.85 to 5.29 between 31 Aug and 19 Oct. Over 28 days, CTR fell from 1.38% (7,811/564,148) to 0.87% (4,817/551,619), significant after correcting for 84 ad comparisons. First-party revenue fell from €24,598 to €15,315 (-€9.3k in 28 days) on the same spend (€3,855), and ROAS fell from 6.23 to 3.97 (last week 3.38). Its sibling ad UGC C in the same account held a 1.30% CTR, frequency 1.89 and ROAS 5.64. Paris revenue is -6% to -10% year on year since the week of 5 Oct. Video A explains part of that; Paris organic and brand search are also softer.

findings.title: New York's -€114k is seasonal, not a loss
findings.evidence: New York revenue was €247,294 against €361,664 in the previous period, but €239,496 in the same period last year (+3.3%). The weekly year-on-year figures from 28 Sep are +7.6%, +4.2%, -1.7% and +2.1%. Last year showed the same step down from about €92k to about €56k a week at the end of September. The fall in brand-search impressions (15,031 to 10,298) matches seasonally lower search demand. No action needed.

findings.title: Barcelona's extra spend (+20% since 28 Sep) bought almost nothing, and the market will overshoot its October budget
findings.evidence: Weekly spend rose from about €4,450 to €5,050–5,350 from the week of 28 Sep. Average weekly paid revenue was €29,612 before and €29,946 after, and total revenue was €62,594 before and €61,727 after. That is roughly +€850 a week of spend for about +€330 of paid revenue (marginal ROAS ≈0.4, with no lift in total revenue). €18,982 of the €20,941 budget is already spent (90.6% with 80.6% of the month gone). At about €760 a day the market finishes about €2.6k over budget.

findings.title: Brand search is mostly paying for buyers who would have come anyway (Milan natural experiment)
findings.evidence: Milan brand search was off from 16 to 29 Aug. Market revenue was €113,208 in the 14 days before, €104,031 while it was off and €101,633 after it came back. Organic plus direct rose from €45,297 to €58,833 while it was off. Using the before/after average (€107.4k) as the baseline, the pause cost about €3.4k against €18.8k of revenue the campaign normally claims, so roughly 18% of it is incremental. That is an incremental ROAS of about 4.4 on €774 of spend, against a reported ROAS of about 24. Brand search costs €19,753 per 28 days across all markets. It is probably still worth running, but its reported ROAS of 11–21 should not drive budget decisions. This rests on one 14-day episode in one market.

findings.title: TikTok and Meta overclaim revenue; TikTok and generic search are the weakest first-party returns
findings.evidence: Over 28 days, TikTok claimed €173,854 against €102,324 first-party (1.70x) on €36,328 of spend, so first-party ROAS is 2.82. Meta claimed €705,389 against €521,355 (1.35x). Google claimed €432,632 against €400,292 (1.08x). Generic search costs €28,128 per 28 days at ROAS 1.98–3.33 in every market. Without margin data we cannot say whether these are profitable.

findings.title: Mexico City is selling out its small capacity; extra spend on generic search and TikTok there is wasted
findings.evidence: Edition 28 is 98.8% sold (250/253) and Edition 29 is 67.1% sold at 64.3% of its window, so the market is limited by capacity, not demand. Spend nearly tripled (€1,805 to €4,929). Generic search returned €289 on €699 (ROAS 0.41) and TikTok €620 on €921 (0.46–0.89): €1,620 of spend for about €909 of revenue. Against earlier launches at the same age (week 7), Mexico City made €11,061 against €32,028 for Miami and €32,093 for São Paulo, with revenue/spend of 7.4 against 10.4 and 8.6. It is behind, but on far less spend and capacity. Too little data to judge its long-term potential; at least another 8 weeks of history are needed.

findings.title: London paid social is now about 38% more expensive per impression; total revenue held because email doubled
findings.evidence: From the week of 28 Sep, London Meta and TikTok impressions fell about 28% on unchanged spend. For Video A, CPM went from about €7.0 to €9.7, and CTR was steady at about 1.4%. Paid Meta revenue fell from €86,835 to €56,104 and TikTok from €17,363 to €11,430. In the same week, email revenue jumped from about €11k to €21k a week (€42,321 to €86,111 over 28 days). London's total revenue is flat (-3%) and up about 4% on last year. Either auction costs rose in London or email is now taking last-click credit for buyers paid social reached. We can't tell which from this data.

recommendations.action: Monday morning: treat the Amsterdam and Berlin iOS checkout as a P1 incident. Put an iOS Safari order through in each market and check the payment methods (Apple Pay, iDEAL, Klarna, card) and whatever was released or changed on 6–7 Oct. Roll back or fix. Until it is fixed, show a visible 'pay by card' fallback on iOS checkout.
recommendations.why: iOS checkout-to-order fell from about 65% to about 22% overnight on 7 Oct, only in these two markets and only on iOS. Android and desktop are unchanged, so the cause is technical, not demand.
recommendations.expected_impact: Recovers about €4.7k of revenue a day (about €130k per 28 days), and lifts Berlin and Amsterdam back to roughly flat year on year.
recommendations.how_to_measure: iOS checkout-to-order rate in Amsterdam and Berlin over the last 7 days. Currently 22.9%; it should return to about 65%.

recommendations.action: Run a 12-day sell-out push for Madrid 'Autumn special': send a dedicated email to the Madrid list and run a Meta ad pointing at the product, paid for from Madrid's roughly €900 of unspent October budget plus early November budget. Consider a time-limited offer in the last 5 days.

questions_for_owner: What was released or changed on the checkout or payment provider on 6–7 Oct? Are Amsterdam and Berlin on a different payment setup (e.g. iDEAL, Klarna, a local Apple Pay configuration) from the other markets?
What is the gross margin per order? Without it we can't say whether TikTok (first-party ROAS 2.8) and generic search (about 2.2) make money.
Did the London email programme change around 28 Sep (more sends, new flows, a discount)? Email revenue doubled the same week paid social revenue fell.
Who decided to raise Barcelona spend from 28 Sep, and against which goal?
Can Madrid 'Autumn special' get its own ad set and email, and is a time-limited discount allowed for it?
Can Mexico City editions get more capacity? Paid demand there is limited by capacity, not by budget.

memo.headline: Spend and traffic held steady, but three problems inside single markets cut qualified leads by 11% (1,014 → 902): France's mobile form has been failing since about 20 Sep, the German "Before and after" ad now brings in leads that almost never get a demo, and Italy's sales team stopped calling leads quickly at the end of August.

data_sufficiency.explanation: There is enough volume to be confident about the three main problems. France's mobile form went from 261 submits out of 350 starts to 77 out of 343. The DE2 ad went from 41 qualified out of 104 leads to 5 out of 106. Italy went from 276 qualified out of 501 leads to 161 out of 500. All three stay significant after correcting for the 10 markets and 30 ads I scanned. Every other market-level change this period is noise once corrected (DE overall p_adj 0.25, PL p_adj 0.69, IT period-on-period p_adj 1.0). Won deals for October are understated because those leads have had less time to close (average 7.5 days to win), so treat won counts as provisional. The link between contact speed and qualification is observational: reps may call promising leads first, which would inflate the gap.

kpis.name: Ad spend
kpis.note: Flat (-1.4%). No agent actions this period.

kpis.name: Leads (all channels, site forms)
kpis.note: -7%. France alone lost 139 leads (275 → 136). meta_form_leads = 0: every lead comes through the website.

kpis.name: Blended spend per lead
kpis.note: Well under the 10 EUR target overall. France is the only market above target: 11.97 EUR, up from 5.94.

kpis.name: Qualified (demo sent)
kpis.note: -11%. Qualification rate 48.7% vs 50.8%.

kpis.name: Spend per qualified lead
kpis.note: DE2 is at 122.86 EUR per qualified lead this period (614.32 EUR / 5).

kpis.name: Won deals
kpis.note: Won value 110,000 vs 128,000 EUR. October leads are still maturing, so some of this gap will close.

kpis.name: Form errors / form starts
kpis.note: Almost all of the increase is French mobile (189 errors on 274 mobile starts this period).

findings.title: France: the mobile form on /fr/ has been broken since about 20 Sep, cutting French leads in half
findings.evidence: Market-level submit/start fell from 275/431 (63.8%) to 136/384 (35.4%), significant after correcting for 10 markets. Mobile only, before vs after 20 Sep: 261/350 (74.6%) vs 77/343 (22.4%), with 234 form errors. Desktop over the same dates: 103/136 vs 93/142, directional only (p=0.06). Traffic and form starts barely moved (4,358 → 4,277 sessions). Search visitors to /fr/ are hit too (46 submits from 135 starts). Daily data shows errors jumping from 20 Sep onward. French qualification of the leads that do get through is normal (75/136, 55%). At the old mobile rate, this period's 274 mobile starts would have produced about 204 submits instead of 64, so roughly 140 leads were lost.

findings.title: Germany: the DE2 "Before and after" ad still brings in leads, but almost none get a demo, starting mid-September
findings.evidence: DE2 lead→qualified fell from 41/104 (39.4%) to 5/106 (4.7%), significant after correcting for 30 ads. Weekly: 9 qualified out of 24 leads in week 37, 3/17 in week 38, then 0/25, 0/23, 2/22 and 3/36. Everything upstream is unchanged: CTR 1.15% → 1.19%, mobile sessions 1,152 → 1,134, submits 104 → 106. Contact speed is not the cause: 70 of 106 DE2 leads were reached within 2 h. The drop hits all four sectors equally. DE1 (36/55) and DE3 (41/77) are normal. Germany's market-level drop (186/359 → 146/337) is not significant on its own (p_adj 0.25); it is entirely DE2. The data does not show why. A changed audience or placement, or junk/bot submissions, are the likely suspects.

findings.title: Italy: since about 31 Aug, leads are contacted much later and qualify far less often
findings.evidence: Share of Italian leads called within 2 h: 299/501 (59.7%) from 6 Jul to 30 Aug vs 69/500 (13.8%) from 31 Aug to 25 Oct. Average time to first contact went from about 19–24 h to about 41 h. Lead→qualified over the same windows: 276/501 (55.1%) vs 161/500 (32.2%). Both changes are significant after correcting for 10 markets. Every other market still calls about 60% of leads within 2 h. Because the break predates both comparison periods, Italy looks stable period on period (90/261 vs 71/239, no detectable difference), so the standard weekly comparison hides it. Italian ads and traffic are normal (239 leads at 5.74 EUR each), but spend per qualified lead is 19.32 EUR vs 10.42 in Spain.

findings.title: Leads called within 2 hours qualify at three and a half times the rate of slower ones
findings.evidence: This period: 732/1,018 (71.9%) qualified when contacted within 2 h vs 170/836 (20.3%) when slower, significant. Earlier periods show the same gap: outside Italy since 31 Aug, 72.0% vs 20.6%. Inside Italy, 82.6% (n=69) vs 24.1% (n=431). Caveat: this is observational. Reps may prioritise leads that look promising, which would inflate the gap.

findings.title: Creative mix: "Before and after" is the cheapest ad everywhere except DE2
findings.evidence: All time, "Before and after" ads cost 5.35–6.20 EUR per lead and 10.97–15.35 EUR per qualified lead. "Owner story" ads cost 8.56–12.26 EUR per lead (FR1 12.26, NL1 12.02, PT1 11.66 are above the 10 EUR target). Spend is split about equally across the three ads in every market. I did not run per-ad significance tests for this, so treat it as descriptive.

findings.title: Other market moves this period are noise
findings.evidence: PL qualification 113/176 → 90/165: directional only, p_adj 0.69. DE market-level: p_adj 0.25, explained by DE2. AT, BE, ES, IE, NL and PT changed by only a few leads. The /nl/oferta vs /nl/oferta-b pages (desktop, direct traffic) had 22 and 17 sessions, far too little to judge.

recommendations.action: Fix the mobile form on /fr/ this week. Reproduce it on iOS and Android phones, look at what changed around 20 Sep (field validation, phone or postcode format, consent checkbox, script deploy), and confirm a real test submission reaches the CRM.
recommendations.why: 189 of the 274 French mobile form starts this period ended in errors. Mobile submit/start fell from 74.6% to 22.4% while traffic held, so the FR budget (1,627.52 EUR/period) now buys leads at 11.97 EUR, double the old rate.
recommendations.expected_impact: About 140 more French leads per 4 weeks, back to the previous ~275. At France's 55% qualification rate, that is roughly 75 more demos sent, with no extra spend. Search traffic to /fr/ recovers as well.
recommendations.how_to_measure: Daily FR mobile form_errors/form_starts in web_sessions should fall back to about 14% (48/350 before 20 Sep), and submit/start should return to about 70%+ within a week of the fix.

recommendations.action: Get Italy's sales team back to calling leads within 2 hours. Find out what changed around 31 Aug (rep leaving or on holiday, routing rule, notification broken) and assign cover or route Italian leads to the shared queue.
recommendations.why: Italy's within-2h contact share fell from 59.7% to 13.8% and qualification fell from 55.1% to 32.2% at the same time, while ad performance was unchanged. Everywhere else, leads called within 2 h qualify about 72% of the time vs about 20% for slower ones.
recommendations.expected_impact: If Italy returns to its July–August qualification rate on about 239 leads per period, that is roughly 60 more demos sent per 4 weeks (from 71 to about 130) at zero media cost.
recommendations.how_to_measure: Weekly IT share of leads with hours_to_contact ≤ 2 (target ≥ 55%) and IT lead→qualified rate (target ≥ 50%) in v_qualified.

recommendations.action: Cut DE2 "Before and after" to minimum budget (or pause it) and move its ~615 EUR per period to DE3 and DE1. In parallel, check the DE2 ad set in Ads Manager for changes around 14–20 Sep (audience, Advantage+ placements, Audience Network, URL or UTM), and sample a few DE2 leads in the CRM for junk patterns.
recommendations.why: DE2 produced 5 qualified leads from 106 this period: 122.86 EUR per qualified lead vs 15.51 for DE3 and 17.24 for DE1. Its clicks and form fills look normal, which points to lower-quality traffic or spam rather than a site problem.
recommendations.expected_impact: At DE3's rate, the same budget would buy roughly 35–40 qualified leads instead of 5. It also frees the German sales team from about 100 dead leads per period.
recommendations.how_to_measure: Germany's qualified count and spend per qualified lead next period. If DE2 is kept on a small budget for diagnosis, its lead→qualified rate should rise from about 5% back toward the ~39% it had before September.

recommendations.action: Set up an alert that flags any market where weekly form errors/form starts exceeds 25%, or the within-2h contact share drops below 40%, and send it to the marketing and sales leads.
recommendations.why: Both the France and Italy problems ran for 4–8 weeks before being caught. Italy's problem is invisible in the standard period-on-period comparison because it started before the comparison window.
recommendations.expected_impact: Catches the next break within a week instead of a month.
recommendations.how_to_measure: The alert fires on the historical France (from 20 Sep) and Italy (from 31 Aug) data when backtested.

recommendations.action: Once DE2 is resolved, gradually shift budget within each market from "Owner story" toward "Before and after" and "Prices carousel", starting with FR1, NL1 and PT1, which are above the 10 EUR target. Keep total spend flat.
recommendations.why: "Before and after" ads have the lowest cost per lead and per qualified lead all time in every market. Budget is currently split equally across the three ads.
recommendations.expected_impact: Lower blended spend per qualified lead. The size is not quantified because I did not test per-ad differences.
recommendations.how_to_measure: Spend per qualified lead per market, period on period, with compare_rates on lead→qualified before shifting more.

experiments.hypothesis: Calling a lead within 2 hours causes higher qualification, rather than reps simply calling their best leads first.
experiments.variant: Italy, after the staffing fix: alternate incoming leads (odd/even lead number). Version B gets a guaranteed call within 2 h; version A gets the normal queue.
experiments.metric: Lead → qualified (demo sent) rate per arm.

experiments.hypothesis: A refreshed German "Before and after" ad, with the pre-September audience and placements restored, brings back lead quality while keeping the low cost per lead.
experiments.variant: Version B is a duplicate DE2 ad set with manual placements (Feed/Stories only) and the original audience. Version A is the current DE2 at equal budget. Run it only if the Ads Manager check does not reveal an obvious change to simply revert.
experiments.metric: Lead → qualified rate per ad (sized to detect 5% → 25%).

questions_for_owner: What changed on the French site or form around 20 Sep (deploy, new field, consent tool, phone validation)?
Did anything change in the DE2 ad set around 14–20 Sep (audience, placements, Advantage+ settings, budget optimisation, destination URL)? Do the DE2 leads look like junk or spam in the CRM?
Who handles Italian leads, and did anything change on that team or in lead routing around 31 Aug?
What is /nl/oferta-b, and who is sending direct traffic to it? Is it an intended test? At 17 sessions it cannot be judged yet.

memo.headline: Spend, traffic and lead volume held steady, but three separate breakdowns are wasting money: the French mobile form has been failing since about 20 Sep, Italian leads have been contacted about twice as slowly since 31 Aug, and DE "Before and after" leads stopped qualifying around 20 Sep.

data_sufficiency.explanation: All three problems are large, start abruptly and pass significance tests after correcting for the number of segments scanned: FR mobile form completion 61% → 28% (n≈300 form starts per period), IT qualification 52% → 26% (n≈250 leads per month), DE2 qualification 37% → 5% (n≈108 leads per period). The data shows where and when each one started, not why, so the causes need answers from the owner (see questions). The link between contact speed and qualification is observational. Sales may reach the most promising leads first, so the true effect of speed is probably smaller than the 25% vs 73% gap. Won deals in this period are close to complete, because the average time to win is about 7.6 days, but leads from the last week are still closing.

kpis.note: Well under the 10 EUR target at account level. The CPL target hides the problems, which happen after the lead.

kpis.name: Qualified (demo sent)
kpis.note: -68. Driven by FR (169 → 104), DE2 (40 → 5) and IT, which has been stuck at about 27% since September.

findings.title: FR: the mobile form broke around 20 Sep and is losing about half of French mobile leads
findings.evidence: FR form completion (submits/starts) fell from 64.0% (290/453) to 41.1% (180/438). The drop is significant after correcting for 10 markets. All of it is on mobile: 61.1% (195/319) → 28.1% (85/303), significant. Desktop is unchanged at 70.9% (95/134) vs 70.4% (95/135), no difference. Mobile errors on /fr/ from paid Meta went 63 → 141, and from search 29 → 59. Daily data shows the jump starting on 2026-09-20 (7 errors on 9 starts, against 0–3 a day before). It has lasted every week since, at about 48–61 errors a week. Form starts are steady at about 100–120 a week, so ads and the landing page are fine and the failure is at the submit step. At the old mobile rate, FR would have had about 100 more leads this period. Other markets show no rise in errors.

findings.title: IT: lead contact speed collapsed from 31 Aug, and qualification halved with it
findings.evidence: The share of IT leads contacted within 2 h went from 57–62% (May–Aug) to 10% in Sep and 12.4% in Oct. Average time to first contact went from about 20 h to 42–44 h. The break is in the week of 2026-08-31: 4 fast contacts out of 59 leads, against 29 of 53 the week before. IT lead → qualified went from 52.5% (138/263, Aug) to 26.4% (64/242, Oct), significant after correction. This period IT runs at 27.6% (74/268) against 54.1% (892/1,649) for the other 9 markets, also significant. Ads and the website are not the cause: IT CPL is fine and leads 268 vs 234. In the other markets over the last 8 weeks, leads contacted within 2 h qualified at 72.9% (1,526/2,093) against 24.7% (329/1,333) for slower contact. Within IT, fast-contacted leads qualify at 75.4% (43/57). The brief's period-over-period table hides this because the previous period was already broken.

findings.title: DE: the 'Before and after' ad (DE2) brings leads that no longer qualify, from about 20 Sep
findings.evidence: DE2 lead → qualified fell from 37.4% (40/107) to 4.6% (5/108), significant even after correcting for all 30 ads. Weekly data: 9–20 qualified a week up to the week of 14 Sep, then 0, 1, 1, 0 and 3 from the week of 21 Sep. DE1 (32/62) and DE3 (29/58) are normal. Everything upstream is unchanged: CTR 1.18% vs 1.08%, CPC 0.30 EUR, landing /de/ only, engagement about 40 s per session, and the same sector mix. Contact speed is also unchanged (89 of 144 contacted within 2 h since 20 Sep). Leads are being reached quickly and then marked lost or left at 'Contactado' (lost 70 of 144 since 20 Sep, against 40 of 176 before). DE2 cost 622 EUR this period for 5 qualified leads (about 124 EUR each), against about 20 EUR (DE1) and 22 EUR (DE3). DE as a market (50.1% → 42.4% qualified) is not significant after correction. The problem is this one ad, not Germany.

findings.title: Every other market is stable
findings.evidence: PT qualified rate rose from 50.4% (62/123) to 61.1% (96/157), but that is only directional once corrected for 10 markets (about 335 leads per period would be needed to confirm it). BE leads fell 126 → 95 and won fell 16 → 8, and ES, NL, PL, AT and IE show only small moves. All of these are within normal variation at these volumes, so they should be treated as stable.

findings.title: Across all markets, 'Before and after' is the cheapest creative per qualified lead
findings.evidence: All-time cost per qualified for 'Before and after' runs from 9.87 EUR (AT2) to 14.76 EUR (NL2), and 10.95 EUR in ES2. 'Owner story' runs 16.52–25.40 EUR and 'Prices carousel' 16.18–21.86 EUR. DE2 was in line with this until 20 Sep, which suggests something changed for that one ad, not the creative concept.

memo.headline: Spend was flat, but qualified leads fell from 1,049 to 946 (-10%), and three problems inside three markets explain most of it: the French form fails on mobile since mid-September, leads from the German "Before and after" ad almost stopped qualifying, and Italian leads have been contacted slowly since late August.

data_sufficiency.explanation: There are 28-day periods of about 2,000 leads and 30,000 sessions, and 6 months of history. All three problems hold up after correcting for the number of markets or ads scanned. Limits: (1) Won deals for leads from the last 1–2 weeks are not final yet (average time to win is about 7.5 days), so the drop in won deals (227 vs 248) is overstated. (2) The link between contact speed and qualification is observational: leads called fast may simply have been better leads. (3) Nothing in the hub explains the German Before-and-after ad (DE2) problem. Its delivery, site behaviour and contact speed are all unchanged, so only the team can say what changed. (4) Smaller swings in PT, BE and AT are within noise.

findings.title: France: the form is broken on mobile since about the week of 14 September
findings.evidence: On French mobile, the share of started forms that get submitted fell from 52.5% (167/318) to 22.6% (69/305). That holds after correcting for 10 markets scanned (p≈0). Weekly form errors in France jumped from 10–18 to 45–54 starting in week 38, and stayed there. French desktop is fine (112/139 vs 83/119, which is noise after correction). Both paid and search traffic on /fr/ are hit (search: 66 submits from 153 starts). Leads in France fell from 250 to 181 on the same traffic (4,455 vs 4,516 sessions). At the old mobile rate, about 90 more leads would have come in this period.

findings.title: Germany: leads from the 'Before and after' ad (DE2) stopped qualifying from week 38
findings.evidence: DE2 leads that became qualified fell from 31.5% (34/108) to 4.2% (5/118). That holds after correcting for 30 ads scanned (p≈0). It is the same in all four sectors (after 14 Sep: bar 2/38, clinic 1/39, hair salon 6/54, shop 7/39, against 27–47 per sector before). Nothing upstream changed: click-through rate is 1.13% vs 1.11%, cost per click 0.30 EUR, engaged time about 40 s, the landing page is still /de/, and the form completion rate held. Contact speed is not the cause either: 30 of 60 DE2 leads still in 'Contacted' were reached within 2 h. 53 DE2 leads were marked Lost this period. DE2 spent 638 EUR for 5 qualified leads (about 128 EUR each), against about 15 EUR each for DE2 over its lifetime. Germany as a market fell from 52.7% to 40.4% qualified, which holds after correction. The other German ads, DE1 and DE3, are normal.

findings.title: Italy: leads have been contacted slowly since late August, and qualification fell with it
findings.evidence: In Italy, leads contacted within 2 h fell from 33–44 a week to 6–15 a week from week 35 (24–30 Aug). Average time to first contact went from about 14–22 h to about 36–45 h. No other market changed (all at 16–25 h). Italy's qualified rate was 55.3% (179/324) in weeks 30–34 and 33.7% (168/499) in weeks 35–42, which holds after correction. Since 24 Aug, Italian leads reached within 2 h qualified at 80.6% (83/103), against 25.4% (116/456) for slower ones. This is observational, but it matches the business-wide pattern: 74% of leads reached within 2 h qualify, against 23% of those reached after 24 h. Compared with the previous period alone, Italy's drop (36.9% to 30.4%) is not significant, because the damage started before that period began.

findings.title: 'Before and after' is the cheapest ad concept per qualified lead and per win, and its leads close just as well
findings.evidence: Lifetime figures excluding DE2: 'Before and after' costs 12.46 EUR per qualified lead and 51.74 EUR per win. 'Owner story' costs 19.62 and 80.98 EUR; 'Prices carousel' costs 18.95 and 70.09 EUR. The share of qualified leads that end up won is the same (Owner story 24.2% vs Before and after 24.1%; no detectable difference). So the gap comes from cheaper clicks (0.30 EUR vs about 0.48–0.55 EUR), not from worse leads. The pattern repeats in all 10 markets. This period spend was split evenly: 3,690 / 3,712 / 3,738 EUR.

BE, AT, IE, NL, PL and ES moved by only a few leads each. Too little data to call any of them changed. Confirming a shift of Portugal's size would take about 270 leads per period, roughly two periods of Portuguese volume.

memo.headline: Since 7 October, iOS checkout in Berlin and Amsterdam has been broken: only about 22% of iOS checkouts become orders, against about 64% before. That has cost an estimated €82k of revenue in 19 days, roughly €30k a week, and fixing it is Monday's top priority. Most of the remaining drop since the previous four weeks (New York's -€137k) is the same seasonal dip as last year.

data_sufficiency.explanation: The data runs from 2025-09-01 to 2026-10-25, so last year's same weeks are available for every market except São Paulo, Miami and Mexico City. The iOS checkout break is based on 1,734 Berlin and 1,385 Amsterdam iOS checkouts since 7 Oct and is significant after correcting for 36 market×device comparisons. Paris Video A's fatigue is based on about 290k–420k impressions per window. Two things are less certain. First, whether paid spend actually adds sales: there is only one natural experiment (Milan brand search off for 14 days) and no test for Meta or TikTok. Second, London's email lift and its pricier Meta delivery are directional only. No gross-margin data is available, so a first-party ROAS of about 2 (generic search, TikTok) cannot be judged profitable or not.

kpis.note: -11.4% on the previous 4 weeks, but mostly seasonal. In the 9 markets that also existed last year, revenue is €1.876M vs €1.925M (-2.6% YoY). Leaving out Berlin and Amsterdam, it is +2.5% YoY.

findings.title: iOS checkout broken in Berlin and Amsterdam since 7 Oct: about €82k lost so far, about €30k a week
findings.evidence: Berlin iOS checkout-to-order fell from 64.7% (1,962/3,035, 7 Sep–6 Oct) to 21.1% (366/1,734, 7–25 Oct). Amsterdam fell from 63.9% (1,557/2,437) to 22.4% (310/1,385). Both drops are significant after correcting for 36 comparisons. Both cities broke on the same day (6 Oct about 65%, 7 Oct 18.5%). Android and desktop in both cities are unchanged (about 62–66%), and iOS in the other markets is at 64.1%. At the old rates, about 575 Amsterdam and 755 Berlin orders were lost, at an average order value of about €62: roughly €36k + €46k = €82k in 19 days. YoY revenue went from about +5% to -34% (Berlin, weeks of 12 and 19 Oct) and -30% to -34% (Amsterdam). This is the only part of the decline that is not seasonal. Ad spend kept flowing at about €1,050/day into these two cities while iOS buyers could not pay.

findings.title: New York's -€137k vs the previous period is seasonal, not a problem
findings.evidence: NYC revenue was €236,236 vs €373,659 in the previous period, but €232,668 in the same weeks last year. Weekly YoY was +1.4%, +1.9%, +3.6% and -0.8%. NYC brand search impressions fell from 14,941 to 10,305 at the same spend, which fits lower seasonal search demand. No action needed.

findings.title: Madrid 'Autumn special' will leave about €126k of capacity unsold
findings.evidence: 880 of 2,883 sold (30.5%) with 77.4% of the window gone and 12 days left (ends 6 Nov), at €71.26. Sales are flat at 133–159 units a week (133 in the last 7 days, about 19 a day). At that pace about 230 more sell, leaving about 1,770 units (about €126k). Madrid's regular Editions 29 and 30 sell about 51 a day and are on pace, so demand for Madrid is fine and this product is the problem. Even doubling its pace recovers only about 230 units (about €16k), so expectations should be modest.

findings.title: Paris 'Video A' (PAR-META-1) is fatigued: frequency 1.9 → 5.3, CTR halved
findings.evidence: CTR fell from 1.42% (5,961/420,395 impressions, 31 Aug–20 Sep) to 0.71% (2,065/291,278, 12–25 Oct), significant after 36-comparison correction. Weekly frequency rose 1.90 → 2.41 → 3.13 → 3.85 → 4.57 → 5.29. First-party revenue fell from about €6.5k a week to €3.1k in the last week, ROAS from 6.8 to 3.1, at an unchanged ~€1k a week of spend. That is about €2.7k a week, or about €11k this period, below its earlier level. The other Paris Meta ads hold steady at frequency ~1.9: UGC C has a CTR of 1.30%, ROAS 5.3–6.4.

findings.title: London: email doubled from 28 Sep while Meta and TikTok delivery got about 35% more expensive
findings.evidence: London email went from about €10–11k a week to €22–23k a week (orders 159–178 → 359–375), +€49.9k this period. Over the same weeks, Meta impressions fell from 1,965,498 to 1,437,487 at the same spend (CPM about €7.0 → €9.7). CTR was stable, so the creative is not the problem. Paid Meta revenue fell €81.8k → €58.5k. Total London revenue still rose (+3.5% on the previous period, YoY +1.8% to +9.3% weekly vs -7% to +8% before). The email change looks positive and the rising Meta cost looks external, but why either happened is unknown.

findings.title: Brand search is incremental, but less than its ROAS of about 17x suggests
findings.evidence: Milan brand search was off 16–29 Aug. Organic and direct revenue rose from €44,059 to €55,596 (+€11.5k), recapturing about 58% of the €19,781 the campaign normally gets. Total market revenue fell from €112,629 to €99,408 (-€13.2k), and the period after was €105,184. The likely incremental revenue is roughly €6–13k per 14 days against about €778 of spend. Keep brand search on. Do not read its 15–20x reported ROAS as the value of extra brand spend.

findings.title: Platforms overclaim, TikTok the most; generic search and TikTok have thin first-party returns
findings.evidence: First-party ROAS this period: Google brand 17.3 (€340,835 / €19,746), Meta 4.93 (€536,867 / €108,787), TikTok 2.73 (€99,326 / €36,416), Google generic 2.10 (€59,174 / €28,118). TikTok claims 1.71x what first-party sales show, Meta 1.35x. Mexico City generic search returned €296 on €724 (ROAS 0.41, 5 orders), so the sample is small. Without margin data, the ~2x channels cannot be judged profitable or not.

findings.title: Mexico City is limited by product capacity, not demand
findings.evidence: At week 7 after launch, Mexico City made €12,490 on €1,499 spend (8.3x). At the same age Miami made €29,528 on €3,080 (9.6x) and São Paulo €35,202 on €3,766 (9.3x). Efficiency is close, and the absolute gap matches capacity: Edition 28 had 286 units and sold 95.5%, Edition 29 is on pace (62.6% sold vs 64.3% of the window gone), while Miami's editions have about 1,440 units. Its meta ROAS of 1.2–1.6 is weak, but the samples are small (64 Meta orders).

findings.title: Barcelona is overspending its October budget
findings.evidence: Barcelona has spent €18,895 of €20,296 (93.1%) with 80.6% of the month gone. Daily spend rose from about €645 (mid-Sep) to €750–770. At that rate it overshoots by about €3.1k by 31 Oct. The extra +€2.6k of spend vs the previous period came with only +€2.7k of total market revenue (€247,394 vs €244,647), so the extra money bought little extra revenue.

recommendations.action: Monday: get the dev team to reproduce and fix iOS checkout for Berlin and Amsterdam, starting with whatever shipped on or around 7 Oct (payment method, Apple Pay, localisation, consent banner, app or webview release). Until the fix is live, exclude iOS from the Berlin and Amsterdam Meta and TikTok ad sets.
recommendations.why: Checkout-to-order on iOS fell from about 64% to about 22% in both cities on the same day, while Android, desktop and iOS in other markets are unaffected. It is the largest non-seasonal loss in the data.
recommendations.expected_impact: About €30k a week of recovered revenue (about €82k already lost in 19 days). Excluding iOS also stops paying for traffic that cannot convert.
recommendations.how_to_measure: iOS checkout-to-order rate in Berlin and Amsterdam, last 7 days; it should go back to about 0.64 from 0.22.

memo.headline: Since 7 Oct, iOS checkout in Amsterdam and Berlin has been broken on every channel: only 21% of iOS checkouts become orders, against 64% before. That has cost about €85k in 19 days (about €4.5k a day) and is the main reason the two cities are 36% down on last year. New York's bigger drop is seasonal; it happened last year too.

data_sufficiency.explanation: First-party sales volumes are large: about 37k orders this period and thousands of checkouts per market and device. The iOS checkout break, the Paris creative fatigue and the London cost rise are each far outside chance (p<0.001 after correcting for 36 or 72 comparisons). Incrementality evidence is thinner: there is one natural experiment (Milan brand search off for 14 days) and none for TikTok or Meta. Read conclusions about whether paid spend adds sales as directional only. The website session tables are empty, so landing-page analysis is not possible.

That cost about 1,360 orders, roughly €84k, in 19 days, and it is the biggest fixable leak this month. Madrid's Autumn special is on track to leave about €115k of stock unsold.

data_sufficiency.explanation: Volumes are large: 37,171 orders, 24.0M impressions and €193k spend in the period, with a full year of history for 9 of the 12 markets. The iOS checkout break, Paris creative fatigue and the London price jump on paid social (cost per 1,000 impressions) all hold up statistically or are clear step changes against last year. Three conclusions are only directional. (1) Whether brand search adds sales rests on one 14-day pause in Milan. (2) Mexico City is 7 weeks old and limited by how much stock it has to sell. (3) The cause of London's price jump is not in the data. Seasonality was checked against the same ISO weeks last year. São Paulo, Miami and Mexico City have no prior year.

findings.title: iOS checkout broke in Amsterdam and Berlin on 7 Oct (checkout-to-order step, iOS only)
findings.evidence: Amsterdam iOS checkout-to-order rate fell from 64.3% (1,530/2,378, 7 Sep–6 Oct) to 22.4% (310/1,382, 7–25 Oct). Berlin fell from 66.7% (1,964/2,943) to 23.2% (416/1,795). Both are significant after correcting for 36 market-by-device comparisons (p≈0). Daily rates were 0.56–0.66 up to 6 Oct, then dropped to 0.13–0.30 from 7 Oct in both cities. Android and desktop in the same cities are unchanged (Amsterdam Android 526/818 = 64%; Berlin desktop 488/730 = 67%). iOS in the other 10 markets is 65.2% (10,938/16,774). Order value is unchanged at about €61.7. At the old rates that is about 579 lost orders in Amsterdam and 782 in Berlin, roughly €84k in 19 days (about €4.4k a day). Weekly revenue is now −31% to −33% on last year in Amsterdam and −28% in Berlin, against roughly flat YoY before.

Paid Meta sessions fell from 21,434 to 15,304, paid Meta revenue from €81.3k to €55.7k (−€25.6k), and Meta new customers from 722 to 454. Other markets' prices are flat (New York about €6.0, Paris about €6.0). In the same week London email doubled (orders 718 to 1,489, revenue €44.9k to €92.3k), so London total revenue is still +12% on last year (€358.7k vs €319.4k). memo.headline: Since 7 Oct, iPhone checkouts in Berlin and Amsterdam have been failing. About €86k of orders were lost in 19 days (roughly €4.5k a day), and this is the biggest loss we can fix on Monday. New York's 33% drop is normal for the season, but Madrid's Autumn special is on course to finish with about €135k unsold.

data_sufficiency.explanation: Volumes are large: 59,443 checkouts and 36,958 orders this period, with a year of history to compare against. The iOS checkout drop and the Paris Video A fatigue both stay significant after correcting for the number of segments scanned, and each shows up in two markets or across several weeks. Two things are weaker. Brand-search incrementality rests on a single 14-day natural experiment in Milan, so treat it as directional. TikTok and generic-search incrementality are untested. London's channel mix shift is last-click attribution only.

kpis.note: Down 11.4% on the previous 4 weeks. In the 9 markets that also traded last year, revenue was €1,867,658 against €1,888,192 for the same weeks last year (−1.1%). Leave out Berlin and Amsterdam and those markets are up about 3.7% year on year, so the autumn dip is mostly seasonal and the real loss is the iOS checkout fault.

kpis.note: Up 3.4%. Most of the increase is Barcelona (+€2.9k) and Mexico City (+€3.2k).

kpis.note: The fall comes from seasonality (New York), the iOS checkout fault (Berlin, Amsterdam), Paris Video A fatigue and higher ad prices (CPMs) in London.

kpis.note: 30,511 in the same 4 weeks last year, which included fewer markets.

findings.title: iOS checkout has been broken in Berlin and Amsterdam since 7 Oct: about €86k lost so far, about €4.5k/day
findings.evidence: iOS checkout-to-order before vs after 7 Oct: Berlin 63.96% (1,338/2,092) → 21.18% (388/1,832). Amsterdam 62.97% (1,046/1,661) → 21.97% (326/1,484). Both are different at 95% after correcting for 36 comparisons. The drop starts on the same day in both markets (Amsterdam 52/80 on 6 Oct → 21/81 on 7 Oct; Berlin 63/94 → 24/92). Android and desktop in the same markets are normal, and iOS elsewhere converts at 64.6%. Checkouts and average order value (about €62) did not change, so traffic is arriving and failing at the payment step. At the old rates the 19 days should have produced about 1,393 more orders: Amsterdam ≈609 × €62.6 ≈ €38k, Berlin ≈784 × €61.5 ≈ €48k. This explains why Berlin and Amsterdam fell 22–35% year on year from the week of 5 Oct, after tracking within ±10% before. Last 7 days: 21.9%, not recovering.

findings.title: Madrid Autumn special will finish with about €135k unsold at its current pace
findings.evidence: 833 of 3,048 sold (27.3%) with 77.4% of the selling window gone and 12 days left. Weekly sales are 135, 141, 141, 166, 133, then 117 last week. At about 117/week that adds about 200 units, leaving about 2,000 unsold at €67.56, roughly €135k. Its capacity is about 30% above Madrid's regular editions, which sell about 340–390/week each (Edition 27 sold 2,294 of 2,350). Madrid's other open products are on pace (Edition 29: 59.2% sold at 64.3% elapsed; Edition 30: 29.7% at 31.0%).

findings.title: New York's 33% revenue drop is seasonal, not a problem
findings.evidence: Revenue was €245,833 against €364,701 the previous period, but €233,877 in the same weeks last year (+5%). Weekly year on year: +8.0%, +2.0%, −0.6%, +10.4%. Every channel, including organic, direct and email, fell by the same share, which fits demand rather than a broken campaign. No action needed. Don't cut New York on the falling paid ROAS (6.65 → 4.22).

findings.title: Paris Meta Video A is fatigued: about €4k/week of revenue lost on unchanged spend
findings.evidence: PAR-META-1 frequency rose 1.87 → 5.29 between the week of 7 Sep and the week of 19 Oct. Click rate (CTR) fell 1.37% (1,930/140,583) → 0.62% (830/133,632), significant after correcting for 72 comparisons. Orders fell 104 → 39 a week and first-party revenue €6,253 → €2,325 a week, while spend held at about €950–1,090 a week (ROAS 6.42 → 2.46). Paris UGC C ran in the same weeks at frequency about 1.9, CTR about 1.3% and ROAS 5.75–5.81, so the audience is fine and the creative is worn out. This is Paris's main paid weakness: Meta revenue went from €70.5k to €54.1k.

findings.title: London: ad prices up about 40% since 28 Sep, and email now takes the last click; total revenue is up
findings.evidence: London Meta CPM was €6.84–7.14 until the week of 21 Sep, then €9.71–9.90 from 28 Sep. TikTok went from €4.11–4.29 to €5.81–5.92. Spend was flat, so impressions fell about 28%. In the same week, email revenue jumped from about €10.2k to about €20.9–25.1k a week, while Meta last-click revenue fell from about €20.3k to €12.9–14.8k a week. Total London revenue is up year on year every week (+11.5%, +20.5%, +7.0%, +7.8%), at €350,033 for the period against €313,154 last year. The paid ROAS drop (6.76 → 4.97) is therefore part ad cost and part attribution moving to email, not lost business. Roughly €5k a month of social spend is buying nothing extra because of the CPM rise.

findings.title: Brand search adds about a third of the revenue it claims, but still pays back
findings.evidence: Milan brand search was off 16–29 Aug (14 days). Milan's total revenue went from €102,305 to €96,678 (−€5,627, −5.5%), while the campaign had claimed €16,547 in the 14 days before. Organic and direct rose from €43,759 to €54,204. Revenue recovered to €103,456 once it was back on. That suggests about 34% of claimed brand revenue is incremental, roughly €7.5 per €1 of spend (€753 per 14 days), against a reported ROAS of about 20. Keep brand search, but don't scale it on reported ROAS. This is one experiment, so treat it as directional.

findings.title: TikTok's own revenue figures are 1.71× first-party, and how much it adds is unknown
findings.evidence: TikTok spent €36,248 this period, claimed €166,458 and drove €97,629 first-party (last click). Creator 2 runs at 1.83–3.46 first-party ROAS across established markets, and Creator 1 is similar or slightly better. With no margin data and no holdout, we can't tell whether the €36k a month pays back. Test before cutting or scaling.

findings.title: Mexico City launch is on track against earlier launches, but stock is the limit
findings.evidence: Weeks 0–7 since launch, revenue per € spent: Mexico City 7.08 (€48.6k on €6.9k), São Paulo 7.91, Miami 9.50. Mexico City's Edition 28 sold 263 against capacity 259 (101.5%), and Edition 29 is at 62.1% with 64.3% of the window gone. Mexico's paid ROAS (2.57) is low because organic and brand demand already make up most of its revenue, not because ads are failing. Adding spend won't help while capacity is about 260–370 units per edition.

findings.title: Barcelona will overspend its October budget by about €2.7k
findings.evidence: €18,950 spent of €20,779 (91.2%) with 80.6% of the month gone. The last 7 days averaged €759/day, about €4,550 for the remaining 6 days against €1,829 left. Barcelona spend rose 16% (€18,004 → €20,880) while paid ROAS slipped from 6.36 to 5.76. Its weakest lines are generic search (2.62 first-party ROAS, about €114/day) and TikTok Creator 2 (2.26, about €72/day).

If it isn't fixed within 3 days, move Berlin and Amsterdam Meta/TikTok delivery to Android and desktop until it is.

memo.headline: Since 7 October the iOS checkout in Amsterdam and Berlin has been failing in every channel: checkout-to-order fell from about 64% to about 20%, which has cost about €87k in 19 days (about €4.6k a day). It is the main reason revenue is down on last year; the other established markets are up 1.8% year on year.

data_sufficiency.explanation: Volumes are large: 36.5k orders and €2.26M first-party revenue this period, and €193k spend. The iOS checkout break and the Paris creative fatigue are both significant even after correcting for the number of segments scanned (36 market×device cells and 84 ads). Year-on-year checks exist for 9 of the 12 markets. Miami, São Paulo and Mexico City have no prior year. Brand-search incrementality rests on one 14-day pause in Milan, so it points a direction but proves nothing. London's change in channel mix has no clean control. Gross margin is unknown, so I cannot say whether ROAS of about 2–3 on generic search and TikTok is profitable.

findings.title: iOS checkout broken in Amsterdam and Berlin since 7 Oct: about €87k lost so far
findings.evidence: On iOS, checkouts held steady but orders collapsed starting 7 Oct in both cities. Amsterdam: 51/78 on 5 Oct, then 17/75 on 7 Oct. Berlin: 72/108 on 6 Oct, then 16/107 on 7 Oct. Over 28 days: Amsterdam iOS 689/2,108 = 32.7% vs 1,384/2,200 = 62.9% before; Berlin 991/2,718 = 36.5% vs 1,823/2,835 = 64.3%. Both are significant after correcting for 36 comparisons (p≈0). The last week is 18–20%. Every channel is hit equally (17–26%: direct, email, organic, brand, Meta, TikTok), so the ads are not the cause. Android and desktop in these cities, and iOS in the other 10 markets, are unchanged (62–66%). Missing orders since 7 Oct at the Sept rate × €62 average order: Berlin €48.1k, Amsterdam €38.9k. YoY went from about 0% to -36% (Berlin) and -46% (Amsterdam) in the week of 19 Oct. It is also dragging Edition 29: at the current 18.1 units a day, Amsterdam ends with about 155 of 1,113 units unsold.

findings.title: Madrid Autumn special will leave about 1,700 units (about €118k at list price) unsold

Selling out would need about 163 a day. Unsold value is €136.8k today. It is priced at €69.86, against €59.49 for Madrid Edition 29, which is on pace (62.2% sold vs 64.3% elapsed, 49 a day). No ad or channel in the data is dedicated to this product.

findings.title: Paris 'Video A' (PAR-META-1) is fatigued: frequency doubled, CTR down 38%, first-party revenue down €11.4k
findings.evidence: Weekly frequency climbed from 1.9 in mid-September to 5.29 in the week of 19 Oct. Weekly clicks fell from about 2,000 to 899 on flat spend (about €1,000 a week). CTR is 0.86% (4,929/569,933) vs 1.39% (8,137/585,961), significant after correcting for 84 comparisons. First-party revenue is €14,608 vs €25,976 on the same €4.0k spend (ROAS 3.63 vs 6.42). Paris UGC C runs at ROAS 6.30 with frequency 1.89. Paris is -5% to -13% YoY over the last 4 weeks, and this ad is the identifiable cause.

findings.title: New York's €111k drop is seasonal, not a problem
findings.evidence: New York revenue went from about €91k a week in September to about €58k a week in October. Last year it fell from about €86k to €52–62k in the same weeks. YoY for the last 3 weeks is -1.3%, +7.4% and +7.1%. Brand search impressions fell (14,516 to 10,148) with the same seasonal demand. No action needed.

findings.title: Barcelona spend up 17% with no extra revenue, and October budget will overrun
findings.evidence: Weekly spend rose from about €4.5k to €5.3k starting the week of 28 Sept. Total weekly revenue stayed at €61–65k (the period is €249.6k vs €258.3k) and paid ROAS fell from 6.92 to 5.90. October is 90.4% spent with 80.6% of the month gone: €19,019 of €21,032 at about €761 a day, which projects to about €23.6k, roughly €2.5k over budget. Revenue and ROAS are not proportions, so this rests on the weekly series. On that series the extra €2,975 shows no visible return.

findings.title: Brand search ROAS (14–20x) overstates what it adds; the Milan pause suggests most of those sales come anyway
findings.evidence: Milan brand search was off 16–29 Aug. The campaign had been credited with €18,589 in the 14 days before. During the pause, organic+direct rose from €44,627 to €58,180 (+€13.6k) and total market revenue fell only from €111,479 to €104,444 (-€7.0k). In the 14 days after, with brand back on, total revenue was even lower at €102,750, so the pause's real cost may be near zero. Brand spend across all markets is about €19.8k per 28 days. This is one 14-day pause in one market, enough to justify a test but not a cut.

findings.title: London: paid-social costs jumped 40% from 28 Sept; email took over and total revenue held
findings.evidence: Meta CPM went from about €6.9 to €9.6–9.8 and TikTok from about €4.2 to €5.7–6.0 on flat spend. Meta impressions fell about 30% and Meta first-party revenue dropped from about €19–20k to €12–15k a week. Email revenue rose from about €10–11k to €18–24k a week in the same week. London total stayed at about €85k a week (YoY +6% to +12%), but new customers fell from about 520 to about 450–480 a week. The cause of the cost jump is unknown. This could also hint that London paid social is less incremental than claimed, but the email change confounds it.

findings.title: Platforms over-claim revenue, TikTok most
findings.evidence: Platform-reported vs first-party revenue: TikTok €179,377 vs €105,274 (1.70x), Meta €727,810 vs €539,859 (1.35x), Google €428,685 vs €396,917 (1.08x). First-party ROAS: TikTok 2.9; generic search about 2.2 (about €28.0k spend for €61.2k revenue). Whether those levels pay depends on gross margin, which is not in the hub.

findings.title: Mexico City is behind earlier launches, but supply is the limit, not demand
findings.evidence: At week 7 after launch: Mexico City revenue €10.5k on €1.5k spend (7.1x), vs Miami €28.9k (9.6x) and São Paulo €33.7k (9.1x). Capacity is small: Edition 28 sold 97.1% of 273 units and Edition 29 is ahead of pace (67.1% sold vs 64.3% elapsed). Generic search there returns €306 on €716 (ROAS 0.43).

memo.headline: Since 7 Oct the iOS checkout in Amsterdam and Berlin has been broken (checkout-to-order rate fell from about 64% to 21%). It has cost about €84k in 19 days and is still costing about €4.4k a day, so fixing it is Monday's top job. Without it, like-for-like revenue would be up about 3% on last year.

data_sufficiency.explanation: The main findings rest on large samples. The iOS checkout break uses 4,530 Amsterdam and 5,435 Berlin iOS checkouts. Paris Video A uses more than 550k impressions. Both pass the significance test after correcting for the number of segments scanned. Mexico City is only directional: it has 58 paid Meta orders in 4 weeks, although the conversion gap against Miami at the same age is significant. Brand-search incrementality rests on a single 14-day pause in Milan, so it is an estimate, not a measurement. ROAS figures use last-click first-party sales, and gross margin is unknown, so I cannot say which channels are below break-even.

findings.title: iOS checkout broke in Amsterdam and Berlin on 7 Oct; about €84k lost so far
findings.evidence: Amsterdam iOS checkout-to-order rate: 64.4% (1,983/3,079, 31 Aug-6 Oct) fell to 21.4% (310/1,451, 7-25 Oct). Berlin iOS: 63.4% (2,359/3,722) fell to 20.7% (355/1,713). Both are significant after correcting for 36 market-device segments (p<0.001). The break happened between 6 Oct (Amsterdam 65%, Berlin 61%) and 7 Oct (19% and 25%). Android and desktop in the same markets did not move (about 62-67%). iOS in other markets is flat at 64.8% (10,597/16,363). Checkouts kept coming (about 75-90 a day per market), so demand is intact and orders are failing at payment or confirmation. Lost orders at the old rate: Amsterdam about 624 × €62.5 ≈ €39k; Berlin about 731 × €62.1 ≈ €45k. That is about €84k in 19 days, or about €4.4k a day. Weekly revenue is now 34-36% below the same week last year in both markets, against roughly flat to +4% before 7 Oct, so this is not seasonality.

findings.title: Madrid · Autumn special will expire with about €120k unsold at the current pace
findings.evidence: 822 of 2,875 sold (28.6%) with 77.4% of the window gone and 12 days left (ends 6 Nov). It sold 126 units in the last 7 days, about 18 a day, which projects to about 1,040 sold. That leaves about 1,835 units × €66.18 ≈ €121k unsold, out of €135.9k unsold now. Madrid's regular editions are on pace (Edition 29: 59.1% sold vs 64.3% of the window; Edition 30: 31.6% vs 31.0%). Madrid's total revenue is flat on last year (-2.8% to +0.7% a week), so the special has not added demand. Its capacity looks oversized for the market rather than under-marketed.

findings.title: Paris Video A is worn out: people see it too often and its click rate has more than halved
findings.evidence: PAR-META-1 frequency (average times each person saw the ad) rose from 1.89 to 5.29 over 8 weeks. Click rate went from 1.36% (5,603/413,230 impressions, weeks of 31 Aug-14 Sep) to 0.59% (812/138,754, week of 19 Oct), significant after correcting for 72 ads. Weekly first-party revenue fell from €6,527 to €2,332 on the same ~€1k a week, and weekly ROAS from 6.56 to 2.44. Paris UGC C runs at frequency 1.92 and ROAS 5.82 this period. Money at stake: about €3.5-4k of revenue a week.

findings.title: New York's 30% drop is seasonal, not a problem
findings.evidence: Revenue was €249,013 vs €353,861 in the prior 4 weeks, but €236,452 in the same period last year (+5.3%). The fall starts in the week of 28 Sep in both years (2026: €73.4k, 2025: €65.7k), and weekly YoY has been +2.5% to +3.1% since. Brand-search impressions fell in line with demand (10,374 vs 14,377). No action needed.

findings.title: Mexico City's paid traffic converts at a third of what Miami's did at the same age
findings.evidence: At weeks 4-7 after launch, Mexico paid ROAS is 2.0-2.6, against Miami 5.0-5.3 and São Paulo 2.6-4.1. Weekly revenue at week 7: €10.7k vs €33.7k (Miami) and €32.6k (São Paulo). Paid Meta visit-to-order rate: Mexico 1.32% (58/4,378) vs Miami 4.24% (377/8,902) at the same age, significant. Generic search: 0.59% (4/677), ROAS 0.27. TikTok: 0.79% (12/1,518). Brand search converts normally (12.2% vs 13.6% in Miami now), so the site works. The gap is at visit-to-checkout and the same across all three Meta ads and all devices (about 2% reach checkout), which points at audience or offer, not a bug. Spend nearly tripled (€1,828 to €4,945) while Mexico's products already sell at or ahead of pace on small capacity (Edition 29: 65.2% sold vs 64.3% of the window; Edition 30: 33.4% vs 31.0%).

findings.title: London's Meta and TikTok ads now cost about 40% more per thousand views; the people they bring convert just as well
findings.evidence: From the week of 28 Sep, London Meta and TikTok impressions fell about 30% at flat spend. LON-META-1 got 478,582 impressions for €4,670 vs 681,643 for €4,739, so cost per thousand went from about €6.95 to €9.76. Click rate is unchanged (1.40%), and paid Meta visit-to-order shows no detectable difference (5.92% vs 6.05%). London Meta and TikTok revenue fell from €93.6k to €66.5k on the same spend. At the same time London email revenue doubled (€42.2k to €89.4k; email visits went from about 2.3k to about 5k a week from 28 Sep). London total revenue is up 1.2% on the prior 4 weeks and 6.7% on last year. Part of the paid drop may be email taking the last click from people the ads brought in.

findings.title: Brand search is worth roughly a fifth of what it reports
findings.evidence: Natural experiment: Milan brand search was off 16-29 Aug. Market revenue over the 14 days went from €107,469 before to €104,235 during (-3.0%) and €109,234 after. Organic plus direct rose from €42,337 to €59,482 and absorbed most of the €18,870 that brand search had been credited with. Revenue that actually depended on the campaign was about €3.2-4.1k per 14 days, against €784 spend. That is an incremental ROAS of about 4-5, against the 19-22 reported. Across all markets this period, brand search cost about €19.6k and was credited with about €326k of first-party revenue. Its true contribution is probably near a fifth of that. It still covers its cost, but it is no reason to add budget.
